clue.text: News hits out about married poet, perhaps

parts.note: word in the sense of tidings, as in 'send word'

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
out signals that the letters of hits are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A news report knocking a married poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns HITS into SITH, and 'about' wraps that around M to give SMITH.
explanation.definitionFit: A poet is one example of a skilled crafter of language, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Clean coat used by painter

definitions.meaning: to clean with water is to give it a rinse
a thin layer of diluted paint or ink spread over a surface

explanation.surface: Cleaning up after painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a verb meaning to rinse clean, and a painter's thin translucent layer of colour.

clue.text: Fear losing head for study

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the word for fear is dropped

parts.note: dread is great fear

explanation.surface: An anxious student afraid of losing their head over study.
explanation.definitionFit: To study a text is to pore over it, a synonym.

clue.text: Hurried up after house discussion group

indicators.note: after places the reversed piece behind the word for house

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, a common British type sharing one wall

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: hurried means ran

explanation.surface: Someone rushing upstairs after arriving home to a study group.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' means read upwards; a semi-detached house is a common British home, giving the convention that house can be SEMI.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a small academic class where students discuss a topic together.

clue.text: Contentious topic for children

definitions.meaning: a matter in dispute, a point of debate

explanation.surface: Raising children as a hot-button debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a disputed matter, and a legal word for one's offspring.

clue.text: Some armour needed for the man with a daughter and gun in America

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
piece is American slang for a handgun

explanation.surface: A man and his daughter in the USA, needing armour and a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A headpiece is a helmet, one item in a suit of armour, hence 'Some'.

clue.text: Detectives ought to arrest leading matchmaker

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold, so the detectives' letters hold the next piece

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
up means ahead, as in a team two goals up

explanation.surface: Police should catch the chief matchmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of love whose arrows make people fall for each other.

clue.text: English weakness after credit for crack

indicators.note: after puts the English and weakness pieces behind the credit abbreviation

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
a vice is a moral failing or weakness

explanation.surface: An English failing that follows from taking on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevice is a narrow fissure or crack in rock or a wall, a synonym.

clue.text: Rewarding suitable answer in endless puzzle

indicators.note: in places the next pieces inside the shortened word
endless drops the final letter of the word for puzzle

parts.note: a problem is something to puzzle over
fit means suitable

explanation.surface: Getting the right answer to a never-ending puzzle is satisfying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' acts on a synonym, not on the printed word: the puzzle becomes a problem shorn of its final letter before 'in' takes the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something profitable yields a return, so it is rewarding.

clue.text: Insulting doctor or aged Conservative

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of or and aged are altered

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: An insulting remark about a doctor or an elderly Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a noun but is the verb that rearranges OR AGED into DEROGA.
explanation.definitionFit: Derogatory remarks belittle someone, so they are insulting.

clue.text: Small and friendly crowd on the move

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
warm means cordial and friendly

explanation.surface: A small, friendly crowd moving along together.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is a large moving mass, as of bees or people, a synonym.

clue.text: Dares to go out of the theatre this way?

definitions.text: Dares to go out of the theatre this way?

indicators.note: out means the letters of dares to go are put out of order

explanation.surface: Bold performers sneak out of the theatre by this exit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DARES TO GO. The whole clue is also the definition: performers and their admirers leave a theatre by this back exit.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage door is the theatre's back entrance used by actors, a way out of the building.

clue.text: Go in using jemmy, being resourceful

parts.note: to go in is to enter
a jemmy is a burglar's crowbar, used for prising things open

explanation.surface: A burglar breaking in with a crowbar, showing initiative.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprising people show initiative and resourcefulness, a synonym.

clue.text: Leaders seeing behaviour with soldiers on last of manoeuvres

parts.note: conduct means behaviour
OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of manoeuvres

explanation.surface: Commanders judging troops' behaviour at the end of exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: Conductors lead orchestras, so they are leaders in music.

clue.text: The achievement of a teetotaller isn't commonly welcoming people

parts.note: TT is the abbreviation for teetotal, someone who abstains from alcohol

indicators.note: welcoming means the colloquial contraction takes in the next piece

parts.note: ain't is the colloquial form of isn't
men means people

explanation.surface: A non-drinker's triumph is not usually friendly to others.
explanation.definitionFit: An attainment is something accomplished, an achievement.

clue.text: Exposed rock group's work around criminal court

indicators.note: around means the work's two letters enclose the rearranged ones

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a numbered work, here a band's

indicators.note: criminal suggests wrongdoing, so the letters of court are bent out of shape

explanation.surface: A band's song about a dodgy court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' looks like an adjective for the court but is the anagram signal; 'around' then wraps the opus abbreviation about the result.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is rock showing at the surface, exposed above the soil.

clue.text: Tramping around nursing a grouse

indicators.note: nursing means holding the next letter inside
around means the letters of tramping are turned about

explanation.surface: A hiker walking about while nursing a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges TRAMPING, and 'nursing' holds A within it. 'grouse' looks like a complaint but is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The ptarmigan is a species of grouse of mountain and Arctic regions.

clue.text: Simple and effective angle developed in case of export

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the outer ones
case of means the outside letters of export
developed means the letters of angle are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A neat new approach to export packaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges the angle letters, and 'in' sets them inside the outer pair of export, which 'case of' supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegant solution is neat and economical, simple yet effective.

clue.text: Habitual response to gum without protection?

indicators.note: without protection strips the outer letters, the covering, from the word for gum

parts.note: to gum is to stick things together

explanation.surface: A reflex reaction to chewing gum with no guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without protection' removes the outer S and K from STICK, its protective casing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tic is an involuntary repeated twitch or habit, a habitual response.

clue.text: Notices planted in river area and lake

indicators.note: planted in means the notices go inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
ads are advertisements, notices

explanation.surface: Signs posted beside a river, an area and a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dead Sea is a salt lake between Israel and Jordan, despite its name.

clue.text: Dons may be working after mistakes

indicators.note: after means the working piece follows the mistakes

parts.note: slips are small mistakes
on means working, as with a machine switched on

explanation.surface: University fellows go on working after their errors.
explanation.definitionFit: To don clothes is to put them on quickly; the plain verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Modern entrepreneur's European fashion, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for fashion is given as it is heard

parts.note: to tailor is to fashion or shape clothes

explanation.surface: A European businessman said to be in the fashion trade.
explanation.definitionFit: An online retailer selling over the internet is a typical modern business person.

clue.text: Early Christian job in sales discovered

indicators.note: in places the job word inside the uncovered word
discovered means the word sales loses its outer cover letters

parts.note: a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A first-century believer finding work in retail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' means uncovered, stripping the outer letters from sales; 'in' then houses the job inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles were the twelve original followers of Jesus, the earliest Christians.

clue.text: Company people must welcome company getting verification

parts.note: a firm is a company

indicators.note: must welcome means the people take the next word in

parts.note: a nation is a people
a firm is a company

explanation.surface: A business taking on new staff and seeking proof of who they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Confirmation is proof or validation that something is true, a synonym.

clue.text: Symbol of bear market's origin

parts.note: to tote is to carry or bear

indicators.note: origin means the first letter of market's

explanation.surface: The emblem of a falling stock market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' is the carrying verb, not the falling market.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem or object revered as a symbol of a group.

clue.text: Agents must have nothing for so long

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Spies with nothing left to do for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal Italian farewell, the same as saying goodbye.

clue.text: Fit is imprecise, very lacking

indicators.note: lacking means the word for very is taken out

parts.note: vague means imprecise

explanation.surface: A judgement on whether something fits, vague and short of detail.
explanation.definitionFit: An ague is a fever with shivering; a fit of shaking is one sense.

clue.text: Lapse in supervision

definitions.meaning: an error made by not noticing something
watching over and being in charge of something

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an unintentional omission and management or superintendence.

clue.text: Slim girl's first obsession

parts.note: thin means slim

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of girl's

explanation.surface: A girl's first fixation with staying slim.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a thing about something is an idiom for being obsessed with it.

clue.text: Material that acted as substitute?

definitions.meaning: to sit in is to deputise for someone; the past tense is two words

explanation.surface: Fabric used as a stand-in.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into two: a stand-in has sat in for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a glossy woven fabric, a material for clothes.

clue.text: Naval officer's been on rum, drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering, so the letters of been on rum are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sailor who has been on the rum ration and is now intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Royal Navy, this is the nickname for the first lieutenant, a ship's second-in-command.
